channel.title: SPFI — Solar Platform for Israel
channel.description: Independent, source-based reporting on solar energy in Israel and worldwide. Items are dated by their original source.

item.title: The land paper trail
item.description: Before a solar field appears in the news, it appears in a land record. Israel Land Authority notices from October and November 2026 show where projects are quietly moving.

item.title: Storage moves into planning
item.description: Israel has about 600 MW of batteries and plans for roughly 9,000 MW by 2030. Two drafts this autumn decide where they can go and who is allowed to build them.

item.title: Energized is not operating
item.description: Israel’s biggest AgriPV announcements of the autumn are planning permissions and tender wins. Here is what each one actually allows, and what it doesn’t.

item.title: Targets against delivery
item.description: Israel plans to triple its renewable capacity by 2035. In 2026 it is connecting less solar than in any year since 2020, while rooftop homes boom.

item.title: One roof, many users
item.description: A warehouse roof powering three shopping centres. An orchard powering a fruit-sorting hall. Three countries show how to use solar where it’s needed, not only where it fits.

item.title: When “dual use” loses the harvest
item.description: A Chinese wheat field lost over 40% of its yield under a solar array. A Californian lettuce field did better in summer. The difference is the lesson for Israel.

item.title: Shade as public infrastructure
item.description: Israel is paying towns to roof their sports courts with solar panels. The first test is whether the result is a good public space, not only a power plant.

item.title: China locks up the recipe, not the panels
item.description: China has proposed banning exports of its most advanced solar-manufacturing know-how. Israeli projects can still buy panels. Israeli factories and licensing deals may find the door closing.

item.title: The grid decides
item.description: Three Electricity Authority moves in October and November 2026 decide which solar projects can connect, how much they earn, and who pays when the grid can’t take their power.

item.title: The kibbutz vote
item.description: A new procedure for kibbutzim and moshavim sends land deals to the general assembly before signing. For farm solar, the members’ meeting becomes part of the project.

item.title: Huawei’s expo announcement puts grid-forming controls alongside AI
item.description: The company describes solar, storage and charging products at IDEE 2026. Their common technical question is how power electronics can help a grid remain stable.

item.title: Beyond Energix’s Lithuania deal: what a hybrid project still has to deliver
item.description: A reported acquisition prompts a closer look at the separate roles of wind, solar and storage—and the difference between a project plan and output.

item.title: AgriPV gets a referee
item.description: Israel has drafted the rules that decide whether farming under solar panels is real. The penalties are financial, and the last step is dismantling.

item.title: Australia’s solar recycling challenge begins before the recycling plant
item.description: A national pilot is designed to test how used panels reach processors. Collection, transport and responsibility matter alongside recovery technology.

item.title: An energy shock can change policy before it changes emissions
item.description: Policies, investment and greenhouse-gas estimates tell different parts of the 2026 energy story. Reading them together prevents premature conclusions.

item.title: A tidal-energy forecast needs a scale—and a shoreline
item.description: MarketsandMarkets projects a larger market by 2031. The announcement offers a starting point for understanding a marine technology, not a measure of electricity already supplied.

item.title: Before a solar garden, listen to the people who will use it
item.description: A North Carolina student project places crop measurements alongside residents’ needs.

item.title: A French farming cooperative enters the solar project conversation
item.description: VIVESCIA and TSE plan to develop agrivoltaic projects together in the Grand Est region.

item.title: What a shaded tomato can tell California's solar researchers
item.description: Early observations at UC Davis show why crop protection and crop growth must be measured together.

item.title: Counting the work sheep could bring to a Michigan solar site
item.description: An MSU scenario explores grazing and vegetation management, with an important distinction between economic activity and farm profit.

item.title: One tender, many surfaces
item.description: Israeli councils have stopped buying solar one roof at a time. Framework tenders now bundle farms, reservoirs, cycle paths and batteries, and one shows what happens when nobody finishes the job.

item.title: What happens when solar panels meet the ground?
item.description: A Fresno water-treatment plant is trying a design that removes the steel rack. The engineering story moves from supporting panels to managing an entire site.

item.title: What happens when a solar roof becomes a garden?
item.description: Bradfield’s roof offers a promising cooling story—and a lesson in separating measurements from models.

item.title: A rooftop tariff proposal raises a question: what is solar electricity worth, and when?
item.description: A reported change for 2027 is a reason to examine payment rules and energy timing—not a confirmed new tariff.

item.title: Stored solar heat reaches the coffee roaster
item.description: A US laboratory demonstration connects solar electricity with process heat.

item.title: The periphery land law: who gets the profit?
item.description: A new law lets Israel’s poorer peripheral towns ask for state land for solar without a land tender. Environmental groups warned about open space; the final text tries to balance both.

item.title: Reservoirs, government roofs and the birds
item.description: Water reservoirs look like the perfect solar surface: flat, unused, owned by the state. A new Israeli wildlife study says they are not empty.

item.title: The alpacas with a second job beneath solar panels
item.description: A New York farm’s experience reveals the people, grazing work and agreements behind a shared solar landscape.

item.title: Dimona solar project clears a financing milestone
item.description: A project participant reports financial close for the planned 265 MW facility. The announcement advances the construction story; it does not establish electricity generation.

item.title: Why a canopy starts two goals down
item.description: Solar canopies cost more than roofs and produce less per square metre. The Dutch government’s answer is to build them big and wire them to nearby industry.

item.title: After a record solar year, the grid becomes the story
item.description: SolarPower Europe's 2026 outlook reports another major expansion. Reading the numbers properly reveals why installation totals and useful electricity are different measures of progress.

item.title: Who gets a say in the solar landscape
item.description: In New Zealand, a solar farm’s fate turned on fire risk, glare and a conflict of interest. In the Netherlands, researchers asked what makes a solar field feel like a landscape. Both lessons point to process.

item.title: Two layers of sunlight: reading a solar-module record
item.description: Trinasolar reports a 907-watt tandem module. The result is a useful opening into how solar cells share the spectrum—and what still separates a test from a dependable product.

item.title: In Egypt, a small solar pilot asks a larger water question
item.description: A South Sinai project brings farming and electricity together; its water benefits still need measurement.

item.title: Saving electricity in a block of heat
item.description: Antora is using hot carbon blocks to supply industrial energy. A South Dakota project shows why a heat battery must be read differently from an electricity battery.

item.title: A battery built for the hours after sunset
item.description: CMBlu's water-based storage offers a different route from lithium-ion. Understanding it means separating chemistry, hours of delivery and evidence from deployment.

item.title: Can a greenhouse share its sunlight with solar panels?
item.description: REGACE explores electricity inside working greenhouses—and shows why a big potential figure needs careful reading.

item.title: Israel’s AgriPV evidence gap
item.description: Israel is writing AgriPV rules for thousands of dunams. The public, measured evidence for how Israeli crops behave under panels still fits on a few pages.

item.title: Ma'ale Gilboa's grapes put solar shade to a field test
item.description: An early harvest study shows why a farming partnership needs careful crop measurements.

item.title: Solar shade needs more than one season of testing
item.description: A Massachusetts experiment challenges promises of a universal crop benefit.

item.title: The neighbours who helped a shared roof become a solar project
item.description: Early agreements in Be'er Sheva and Karmiel reveal the organizing work behind apartment-building solar.

item.title: The work after installation: cleaning solar panels at Ketura
item.description: Ecoppia's 2014 Ketura Sun deployment offers an Israeli case study in the service work behind solar electricity, where dust, water and maintenance meet.
